source.role: Obsidian plugin: define one or more named 'calendar sets', each enabling day/week/month/quarter/year granularities with its own format/folder/template, create-or-open notes for those granularities, index existing notes into a cache, and expose a small API (openPeriodicNote, calendarSetManager, settings) for other plugins such as obsidian-calendar-plugin. Personal fork matisnape/obsidian-periodic-notes, branch main, HEAD e332ac6, installed in this vault under dev plugin id periodic-notes-anks.

modules.name: main.ts
modules.role: Plugin entry point: lifecycle, ribbon/command (re)registration, settings load/migrate, and the public methods other plugins call (openPeriodicNote, createPeriodicNote, getPeriodicNote(s), isPeriodic, findAdjacent, findInCache).

modules.name: commands.ts
modules.role: Builds the 5 per-granularity commands (open/next/prev/open-next/open-prev) and the adjacent-note jump/open logic that backs them.

modules.name: modal.ts
modules.role: Ribbon right-click context menu (showFileMenu, used) and a PeriodicNoteCreateModal (defined, never used).

modules.name: icons.ts
modules.role: Raw SVG path strings for the calendar-day/week/month/quarter/year ribbon icons, registered via addIcon() in main.ts.

modules.name: types.ts
modules.role: Core domain types: Granularity union, granularities[] order array, PeriodicConfig (per-granularity settings) and CalendarSet (a named bundle of PeriodicConfig per granularity).

modules.name: calendarSetManager.ts
modules.role: CalendarSetManager class (active-set lookup, active/inactive granularities, rename) plus the one-time legacy-settings migration functions and the private ILegacySettings type used only to detect them.

modules.name: settings/index.ts
modules.role: ISettings interface, DEFAULT_SETTINGS, DEFAULT_PERIODIC_CONFIG, and the PluginSettingTab that mounts the Svelte settings router.

modules.name: settings/utils.ts
modules.role: Settings-store updater functions (create/delete/rename/set-active calendar set, clearStartupNote, findStartupNoteConfig) and helpers for the core Daily Notes plugin and locale/week-start option lists.

modules.name: settings/validation.ts
modules.role: Format/folder/template validators plus the 'fragile basename' complexity check and the format-aware getDateInput() used by the cache when matching nested-path formats.

modules.name: settings/localization.ts
modules.role: Reads/writes Obsidian's vault-level localeOverride/weekStart config, mutates the global moment.js locale and week-start (window.moment.updateLocale), guarded to run once per session.

modules.name: settings/stores.ts
modules.role: The `router` writable Svelte store driving the settings mini-app: a breadcrumb path plus an eState bag used for one-shot signals like 'focus this field on mount'.

modules.name: obsidian.d.ts
modules.role: Ambient type augmentation of the 'obsidian' module: Workspace custom events (periodic-notes:settings-updated, periodic-notes:resolve), VaultSettings.localeOverride/weekStart, internal-plugin and nldates-obsidian typings this plugin relies on but Obsidian doesn't ship types for.

modules.name: utils.ts
modules.role: Date/template/path grab-bag: template-token expansion, format lookup/fallback helpers, the strict-then-prefix date parser (getDateWithPrefixFallback), note-creation path + folder auto-create, and relative-date humanization.

modules.name: parser.ts
modules.role: getLooselyMatchedDate(): regex-only day/month/year guesser used as the cache's last-resort fallback when a file matches no configured folder/format at all.

modules.name: cache.ts
modules.role: PeriodicNotesCache: the in-memory index of every file matched to a (calendar set, granularity, date), built on layout-ready, kept live via vault/metadata event listeners, and read by every note-lookup and adjacent-note capability.

modules.name: constants.ts
modules.role: Default moment.js format strings per granularity (DEFAULT_FORMAT) and human-readable display formats (HUMANIZE_FORMAT).

modules.name: switcher/switcher.ts
modules.role: NLDNavigator: a SuggestModal that turns natural-language date queries (via the nldates-obsidian plugin) plus a set of hand-written relative-date regexes into periodic-note suggestions; Tab hands off to RelatedFilesSwitcher.

modules.name: switcher/calendarSetSwitcher.ts
modules.role: CalendarSetSuggestModal: a FuzzySuggestModal listing calendar sets by id; choosing one calls setActiveSet.

modules.name: switcher/fileOptionsSwitcher.ts
modules.role: FileOptionsSwitcher: a SuggestModal stub with a single unimplemented 'Delete file' item. Dead code — never imported or instantiated anywhere in the repo.

modules.name: switcher/relatedFilesSwitcher.ts
modules.role: RelatedFilesSwitcher: lists inexact/prefix-matched notes for a period selected in NLDNavigator; Shift+8 toggles including finer granularities; Tab hands back to NLDNavigator with the query preserved.

modules.name: timeline/manager.ts
modules.role: TimelineManager: mounts/unmounts one Timeline.svelte component per open MarkdownView, keyed on workspace layout-change events; cleans up on plugin unload.

modules.name: timeline/Timeline.svelte
modules.role: The floating 'Today'/'Last week'/etc. badge injected top-right of a periodic note's view; click to expand a 7-day strip; clicking a weekday opens/creates that day's note.

modules.name: timeline/RelativeIcon.svelte
modules.role: Tiny forward-arrow icon shown next to the timeline badge when the current note matched only inexactly (prefix/loose match).

modules.name: ui/suggest.ts
modules.role: Generic Suggest/TextInputSuggest base classes: keyboard nav, popper.js-positioned dropdown, abstract getSuggestions/renderSuggestion/selectSuggestion contract used by FileSuggest/FolderSuggest.

modules.name: ui/file-suggest.ts
modules.role: FileSuggest and FolderSuggest: TextInputSuggest implementations used by the Template and Folder settings fields.

modules.name: settings/pages/Router.svelte
modules.role: Top-level Svelte router for the settings tab: renders Breadcrumbs, then either Dashboard (root) or Details (a calendar set selected), keyed off the `router` store.

modules.name: settings/pages/dashboard/Dashboard.svelte
modules.role: Settings root page: getting-started banner, grid of calendar-set cards with an 'add' button, the timeline-complication toggle, and the vault-wide week-start/locale dropdowns.

modules.name: settings/pages/dashboard/GettingStartedBanner.svelte
modules.role: Onboarding banner: detects the core Daily Notes plugin and offers to disable it; explains the plugin when no legacy daily-note settings exist yet.

modules.name: settings/pages/dashboard/CalendarSets/MenuItem.svelte
modules.role: One calendar-set card on the dashboard: shows enabled granularities with checkmarks, an options menu (set active/duplicate/delete), click navigates to Details.

modules.name: settings/pages/details/Details.svelte
modules.role: Detail page for one calendar set: inline-rename title, active/duplicate/delete options menu, and an accordion of PeriodicGroup entries (one per granularity). Contains the local scroll-guard crash fix.

modules.name: settings/pages/details/PeriodicGroup.svelte
modules.role: One collapsible granularity section inside Details: enable checkbox plus Format/Folder/Template/AllowPrefixMatch/OpenAtStartup sub-settings, using svelte-writable-derived to read/write straight into the parent calendarSets[] array.

modules.name: settings/components/NoteFormatSetting.svelte
modules.role: The Format text field: live-previews the current moment.js format and shows validation error/complexity warnings as you type.

modules.name: settings/components/NoteFolderSetting.svelte
modules.role: The Note Folder text field, backed by FolderSuggest autocomplete and validateFolder().

modules.name: settings/components/NoteTemplateSetting.svelte
modules.role: The Template Path text field, backed by FileSuggest autocomplete and validateTemplate().

modules.name: settings/components/AllowPrefixMatchSetting.svelte
modules.role: Local fork's 'Allow prefix matching' toggle, modeled directly on OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte. New, not upstream.

modules.name: settings/components/OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte
modules.role: The 'Open on startup' toggle; turning it on calls clearStartupNote to enforce vault-wide exclusivity before setting itself.

modules.name: settings/components/{Arrow,Breadcrumbs,Checkmark,Dropdown,Footer,IconButton,SettingItem,Toggle}.svelte
modules.role: Reusable, purely presentational building blocks for the settings mini-app (expand arrow, breadcrumb trail, checkmark, dropdown, footer credit, generic setting-item row, toggle switch) plus IconButton.svelte, which is defined but never imported anywhere.

modules.name: styles.css
modules.role: Global CSS for the periodic-note-create modal, suggestion flair/badges in the switchers, and misc settings-page chrome not covered by component-scoped Svelte styles.

capabilities.name: Calendar set data model
capabilities.description: A CalendarSet is a named bundle (id, ctime) holding one optional PeriodicConfig (enabled, format, folder, templatePath, allowPrefixMatch, openAtStartup) per granularity (day/week/month/quarter/year). ISettings.calendarSets is an array of these; ISettings.activeCalendarSet names the one currently in effect.
behaviour_notes: This is the ONLY live config surface in v0.0.17 — see observation about the dead top-level daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly keys.
A calendar set with zero enabled granularities is valid and shown as 'Not configured' in the dashboard card.
edge_cases: Deleting the last remaining calendar set is disabled in the UI (menu item setDisabled when length === 1), but deleteCalendarSet() itself has no such guard if called programmatically.

capabilities.name: Resolve the active calendar set
capabilities.description: getActiveId()/getActiveSet() read settings.activeCalendarSet and find the matching entry in settings.calendarSets.
behaviour_notes: getActiveSet() throws 'No active calendar set found' if activeCalendarSet doesn't match any entry — there is no fallback-to-first-set here (unlike deleteCalendarSet, which does fall back).

capabilities.name: List active/inactive granularities for the active set
capabilities.description: getActiveGranularities() and getInactiveGranularities() filter the fixed granularities[] order array by whether the active set's PeriodicConfig.enabled is true.
behaviour_notes: Order is always day, week, month, quarter, year (granularities[] in types.ts) regardless of insertion order in the calendar set — this fixes ribbon-icon and command ordering.

capabilities.name: Switch the active calendar set
capabilities.description: The 'Switch active calendar set...' command opens a FuzzySuggestModal of all calendar sets; choosing one calls setActiveSet(id), which writes settings.activeCalendarSet and triggers the settings-store subscription.
behaviour_notes: Switching sets re-runs configureCommands()/configureRibbonIcons() and resets the note cache, because onUpdateSettings fires on every settings.subscribe (main.ts:203-210) and cache.reset() listens for the 'periodic-notes:settings-updated' workspace event.

capabilities.name: Create a new calendar set
capabilities.description: createNewCalendarSet(id, refSettings?) pushes a new CalendarSet built from a default per-granularity config, optionally cloning refSettings (used for duplication). Called both by the dashboard's '+' button (empty defaults) and the 'Duplicate calendar set' menu item (existing set as refSettings).
behaviour_notes: Dashboard auto-generates a unique id 'Calendar set N' by probing for the first free suffix; navigates to the new set's Details page with eState.shouldRename=true so the title is immediately editable.
edge_cases: Also used at plugin-load time to synthesize the very first 'Default' calendar set (see legacy-settings-migration).

capabilities.name: Duplicate a calendar set
capabilities.description: The '...' menu on a calendar-set card or Details page's toolbar builds a '<name> copy' id and calls createNewCalendarSet(newId, existingSet), then navigates to it with shouldRename=true.
behaviour_notes: Thin UI wrapper over create-calendar-set with refSettings — kept as its own capability because it is a distinct, user-visible action (menu item), not because the code differs.

capabilities.name: Rename a calendar set inline
capabilities.description: Details.svelte's title is a contenteditable div; on blur, renameCalendarset(oldId, newId) validates uniqueness/non-empty, updates the CalendarSet.id and activeCalendarSet if it was the active one, then the caller navigates the router to the new id.
behaviour_notes: Throws (and the UI catches + refocuses the field) on an empty or duplicate proposed name; a no-op if the name is unchanged.

capabilities.name: Delete a calendar set
capabilities.description: deleteCalendarSet(id) removes the set from settings.calendarSets; if it was the active set, falls back to calendarSets[0].
edge_cases: settings.calendarSets[0] is accessed unconditionally when falling back — deleting the very last calendar set (bypassing the UI's setDisabled guard) would throw on `.id` of undefined.

capabilities.name: Migrate legacy Daily-Notes / pre-calendar-set settings on first load
capabilities.description: On loadSettings(), if calendarSets[] is empty, the plugin checks (in order): (1) does the raw saved data.json look like the pre-calendar-set ILegacySettings shape (top-level daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly keys)? -> migrateLegacySettingsToCalendarSet builds one 'Default' set from all five. (2) does the core Daily Notes internal plugin have non-empty format/folder/template? -> migrateDailyNoteSettings builds a 'Default' set with only 'day' populated. (3) otherwise create a bare 'Default' set with only 'day' enabled.
behaviour_notes: isLegacySettings() is a structural type-guard on the raw loaded object, not on ISettings — it only fires because ISettings itself no longer declares those fields (see the dead-top-level-keys observation).
edge_cases: Path (1) and (2) are mutually exclusive (else-if): a vault with both legacy plugin-data AND live core Daily Notes settings only migrates the plugin-data shape.

capabilities.name: Add/remove per-granularity commands as the active set changes
capabilities.description: configureCommands() removes the 5 commands for every currently-inactive granularity (app.commands.removeCommand) and (re-)adds them for every active one, every time settings change.
behaviour_notes: Command ids are unprefixed inside commands.ts (e.g. 'open-daily-note') but removeCommand needs the fully-qualified `periodic-notes:open-daily-note` — main.ts hardcodes that prefix, which is the manifest.json plugin id, not the vault's dev-install id (see observation on 'periodic-notes-anks').
edge_cases: Runs on every settings change (every keystroke that updates a Writable-bound field, since svelte-writable-derived triggers the parent store), not only when granularities actually toggle — cheap because addCommand/removeCommand are idempotent, but worth knowing for a merge that batches settings writes.

capabilities.name: Ribbon icon for the first active granularity
capabilities.description: configureRibbonIcons() shows exactly one ribbon icon, for the FIRST granularity (in day/week/month/quarter/year order) that is enabled in the active calendar set. Clicking opens/creates today's note for that granularity; meta/cmd-click opens it in a new split; right-click opens a context menu (showFileMenu) listing every active granularity.
behaviour_notes: If no granularity is enabled, no ribbon icon is shown at all.
Local fork commit a8aa7e4 moved this call out of onLayoutReady into onload() directly so ribbon items register before Obsidian applies its ribbon sort order (upstream fix, already on this branch).

capabilities.name: Ribbon right-click menu: open any active granularity's note
capabilities.description: showFileMenu() builds an Obsidian Menu with one item per active granularity ('Open today's daily note', etc.); clicking opens/creates it.

capabilities.name: Create a periodic note
capabilities.description: createPeriodicNote(granularity, date) formats the filename, reads+expands the configured template, resolves/creates the destination folder, and vault.create()s the file. Returns the created TFile.
behaviour_notes: Uses the ACTIVE calendar set's config/format unconditionally — there is no calendarSet parameter, unlike openPeriodicNote which accepts one.
edge_cases: vault.create() throws if a file already exists at the computed path outside the cache's knowledge (e.g. cache not yet initialized) — no existence check is done here.

capabilities.name: Open (or create) a periodic note
capabilities.description: openPeriodicNote(granularity, date, opts?) looks the note up in the cache for the given (or active) calendar set; creates it via createPeriodicNote if missing; opens it in a new split or the current unpinned leaf.
behaviour_notes: This method is explicitly rebound in onload (`this.openPeriodicNote = this.openPeriodicNote.bind(this)`) — a deliberate signal it's meant to be destructured and called by other plugins without losing `this`.

capabilities.name: Look up the exact periodic note for a date
capabilities.description: Cache.getPeriodicNote(calendarSet, granularity, date) linear-scans that calendar set's cache for an EXACT match (matchData.exact === true) whose date isSame(target, granularity); returns the TFile or null. main.ts:getPeriodicNote and the plugin's public getPeriodicNote are thin wrappers.
behaviour_notes: Only ever returns a note whose match was exact — inexact/prefix matches are invisible here even if allowPrefixMatch is on; those surface only via get-periodic-notes-related.

capabilities.name: List all cached notes for a period, optionally including finer granularities
capabilities.description: Cache.getPeriodicNotes(calendarSet, granularity, date, includeFinerGranularities?) returns every cached entry whose date isSame(target, granularity), either restricted to the requested granularity or (with the flag) any granularity at or finer than it (day <= week <= month <= quarter <= year order via compareGranularity). Used by the related-files switcher and the timeline's '+N' badge.
behaviour_notes: main.ts:getPeriodicNotes (the plugin's public wrapper) carries the author's own '// TODO: What API do I want for this?' comment — treat the includeFinerGranularities boolean-flag shape as unsettled.

capabilities.name: Check whether a file path is a periodic note
capabilities.description: Cache.isPeriodic(path, granularity?) scans every calendar set's cache for an entry at that path, optionally filtered to one granularity. Used by every command's checkCallback to decide whether jump/open-adjacent should be enabled.

capabilities.name: Find the next/previous periodic note of the same granularity
capabilities.description: Cache.findAdjacent(calendarSet, filePath, direction) sorts that calendar set's same-granularity entries by canonicalDateStr (an ISO string) and returns the neighbour one position forwards or backwards.
behaviour_notes: Re-sorts the ENTIRE calendar-set/granularity slice on every call rather than maintaining a sorted structure — fine at personal-vault scale, a hazard if the merged plugin targets much larger vaults.
edge_cases: Includes inexact/prefix matches in the sort, so 'adjacent' can land on a loosely-matched note, not just an exact one.

capabilities.name: Jump to the closest existing adjacent note (no creation)
capabilities.description: 'Jump forwards/backwards to closest <periodicity> note': looks up the active file's cache metadata, calls find-adjacent-note, opens the result if found or shows a Notice ('There's no ... note before/after this') if not.
behaviour_notes: Never creates a note — pure navigation, distinct from open-adjacent-note-command.

capabilities.name: Open the next/previous note by date offset (creating it if needed)
capabilities.description: 'Open next/previous <periodicity> note': computes the active file's date +/- 1 unit of its own granularity and calls openPeriodicNote, creating the note if it doesn't exist yet.
behaviour_notes: Unlike jump-to-adjacent-note-command, this always succeeds (by creating), which is why an older commit (b517af8, 'jump backwards will create new notes') exists upstream distinguishing the two behaviors.

capabilities.name: Find a file's cache metadata (any or a specific calendar set)
capabilities.description: Cache.find(filePath, calendarSet?) looks the path up directly if a calendar set is given; otherwise checks the active set first, then every other set. Wrapped by main.ts's findInCache.

capabilities.name: Auto-open a configured note on vault load
capabilities.description: On workspace.onLayoutReady, findStartupNoteConfig() scans every calendar set/granularity for openAtStartup===true and, if found, calls openPeriodicNote for today's date in that calendar set.
behaviour_notes: Only the FIRST match found (iterating calendarSets then granularities in fixed order) is opened, which is consistent with clear-startup-note-exclusivity enforcing at most one such flag vault-wide.

capabilities.name: Enforce a single startup-note flag vault-wide
capabilities.description: clearStartupNote() walks every calendar set and granularity, clearing openAtStartup wherever it's true. Called by OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte just before setting the newly-toggled one, so turning on one 'Open at startup' switch turns off every other one, across all calendar sets.
behaviour_notes: This is a quiet, easy-to-lose-in-a-merge invariant: the setting's own type (PeriodicConfig.openAtStartup: boolean) does not enforce exclusivity; it's enforced only by this call-site convention.
edge_cases: Only invoked from the toggle's onChange when turning it ON — toggling one OFF does not re-run it (no-op needed anyway).

capabilities.name: Template token expansion
capabilities.description: applyTemplateTransformations(filename, granularity, date, format, templateContents) replaces {{date}}/{{time}}/{{title}} always, plus granularity-specific tokens: day gets {{yesterday}}, {{tomorrow}}, and {{date|time (+/-N unit)(:format)}}; week gets {{sunday:fmt}}..{{saturday:fmt}} (day-of-week relative to the note's week); month/quarter/year get {{month|quarter|year (+/-N unit)(:format)}} anchored to startOf(that unit).
behaviour_notes: The +/-N calc tokens borrow the CURRENT wall-clock hour/minute/second (via window.moment() 'now'), not the target date's own time-of-day, before adding the offset.
Also reused for RE-templating on template-file changes via applyPeriodicTemplateToFile (utils.ts:228-247), not just at creation time.
edge_cases: Regexes are case-insensitive and tolerate arbitrary whitespace inside {{ }}, but a malformed calc suffix (e.g. missing unit letter) simply fails to match and passes the token through unexpanded.

capabilities.name: Resolve creation path and auto-create missing folders
capabilities.description: getNoteCreationPath(app, filename, config) joins config.folder + filename (+.md), normalizes it, and ensureFolderExists() creates every missing intermediate folder via vault.createFolder before returning the path.
behaviour_notes: join()/basename() are a small hand-rolled path.js (credited to @creationix/path.js in a comment) rather than using Obsidian's normalizePath alone — handles multi-segment folder+filename joining with '.' segment stripping.
edge_cases: ensureFolderExists checks only the immediate parent folder existence in one shot (vault.createFolder can itself create intermediate segments in Obsidian's API), not each ancestor individually.

capabilities.name: Strict-then-prefix date parsing (getDateWithPrefixFallback)
capabilities.description: For each candidate format (strictest first): try window.moment(input, format, true) (strict mode) and return isExactMatch:true on the first success. If none succeed strictly, retry every format in NON-strict mode; accept the first result where date.format(format) is a PREFIX of the original input string (isExactMatch:false). Returns {date: null, isExactMatch: false} if nothing matches either way.
behaviour_notes: Local fork addition, commit e50b8e8. The canonical example from the commit message: filename '2026-W07, 09.02 - 15.02.md' does not strictly match format 'gggg-[W]ww', but a loose parse reformats to '2026-W07' which IS a prefix of the filename, so it's accepted as an inexact match.

The prefix check is a plain string startsWith on the REFORMATTED date, not a regex against the original format — so it only works when the format's literal/moment output naturally forms a prefix of real filenames (works well for '<date>, <suffix>' naming, not for '<suffix> <date>' naming).
edge_cases: Whether the inexact-match branch is even allowed to win depends on the caller passing allowPrefixMatch=true (cache.ts gates it, not this function itself — this function always computes and returns the fallback result regardless of the setting).

capabilities.name: Possible-formats expansion for nested-path formats
capabilities.description: getPossibleFormats(calendarSet, granularity) returns [fullFormat] normally, or [fullFormat, basenameOnlyFormat] when the configured format contains a '/' (e.g. 'YYYY/YYYY-MM-DD'), so matching can succeed whether or not the note was later moved out of its dated subfolder.

capabilities.name: Vault-wide loose date guess when no configured format matches at all
capabilities.description: getLooselyMatchedDate(basename) tries, in order, a full YYYY-MM-DD-ish regex, then a YYYY-MM-ish regex, then a bare 4-digit-year regex, returning the first hit as {date, granularity}. Used by cache.resolve() as a last resort per calendar set when no active granularity's folder+format matched the file.
behaviour_notes: A week regex (WEEK_PREFIX) is written but commented out with a TODO about ISO-week ambiguity — week granularity is never guessed loosely.
edge_cases: See observation: this fallback is NOT folder-scoped in the caller (cache.resolve()), so it can match files anywhere in the vault, not just under the calendar set's configured folders.

capabilities.name: Warn when a nested-path format's basename can't uniquely identify a day
capabilities.description: validateFormatComplexity(format, granularity) returns 'loose-parsing' if the format doesn't round-trip through a strict parse at all, or 'fragile-basename' if (for day granularity, with a '/' in the format) the basename portion is missing a day/month/year token letter — surfaced as an inline warning with a frontmatter workaround suggestion in NoteFormatSetting.svelte.
behaviour_notes: getDateInput() (settings/validation.ts:84-98) is the consumer of this classification in the cache path: when fragile-basename, it reconstructs a multi-segment 'path suffix' string (matching the format's nesting depth) instead of just file.basename before handing it to date parsing.

capabilities.name: Validate a format string
capabilities.description: validateFormat(format, granularity) rejects illegal filename characters/control chars/reserved Windows names, and (for day granularity only) checks that formatting 'now' and re-parsing strictly round-trips.
behaviour_notes: The strict round-trip check only runs for granularity === 'day' — week/month/quarter/year formats are only checked for illegal characters, not parseability, at input time (parseability issues there surface later via validateFormatComplexity's 'loose-parsing' warning instead).

capabilities.name: Validate a folder path
capabilities.description: validateFolder(app, folder) accepts empty or '/' as valid (vault root); otherwise checks the normalized path exists in the vault.
behaviour_notes: Only validates existence, not creatability — actual folder creation happens lazily at note-creation time (ensureFolderExists), so a not-yet-existing folder is a UI warning, not a hard block.

capabilities.name: Validate a template file path
capabilities.description: validateTemplate(app, template) resolves the path via metadataCache.getFirstLinkpathDest and reports 'Template file not found' if it doesn't resolve.

capabilities.name: Build the full note-cache index on vault layout-ready
capabilities.description: PeriodicNotesCache.initialize() walks, for every calendar set and every active granularity's configured folder, the folder's file tree (memoized recursion) and runs resolve()+resolveChangedMetadata() on each file, populating cachedFiles: Map<calendarSetId, Map<filePath, metadata>>.
behaviour_notes: Runs once at workspace.onLayoutReady, not at plugin onload — avoids racing Obsidian's own initial vault/metadata indexing.
edge_cases: A folder path that doesn't exist yet (getAbstractFileByPath returns null/undefined) is silently skipped by the memoized recursor's `if (!rootFolder) return` guard.

capabilities.name: Resolve a single file against every calendar set on create
capabilities.description: resolve(file, reason) checks each calendar set (skipping if a frontmatter match already exists for that path), then each active granularity: folder-prefix match, then strict-then-prefix date parsing gated by allowPrefixMatch, then (if nothing matched for any granularity in that set) the vault-wide loose fallback. On a match it caches the metadata, fires 'periodic-notes:resolve', and — if this is a brand-new EMPTY file — auto-applies the granularity's template.
behaviour_notes: Registered on vault 'create' — fires for every new file in the vault, not just ones under a configured folder; the folder-prefix check (`file.path.startsWith(folder)`) is the actual filter.
edge_cases: 'frontmatter supersedes filename': if a path already has a frontmatter-sourced cache entry for this calendar set, the filename-matching branch is skipped entirely for that set (continue calendarsets) — but a NEW filename match can still overwrite an existing filename-sourced entry.

capabilities.name: Re-resolve a file on rename
capabilities.description: resolveRename(file, oldPath) deletes the old path from every calendar-set cache and re-runs resolve() on the new path.
behaviour_notes: Iterates ALL calendar-set caches to delete oldPath (not just the one(s) it was cached under) — harmless but O(n) over calendar sets per rename.

capabilities.name: Resolve a file via a frontmatter date field
capabilities.description: resolveChangedMetadata(file, _, cache) is registered on metadataCache 'changed'. For each calendar set/active granularity whose folder prefixes the file path, if the frontmatter has a string entry keyed by the granularity name (e.g. `day: 2022-02-02`), it's parsed STRICTLY against DEFAULT_FORMAT[granularity] (not the calendar set's configured format) and cached as an exact, matchType:'frontmatter' entry.
behaviour_notes: This is the path referenced by NoteFormatSetting.svelte's warning text ('include `<granularity>: <DEFAULT_FORMAT>` in your template frontmatter') for loose-parsing/fragile-basename formats.
edge_cases: Ignores the calendar set's own configured format and its allowPrefixMatch flag entirely — see observation on the asymmetry with the filename-based resolve() path.

capabilities.name: Rebuild the cache whenever settings change
capabilities.description: The cache listens for the 'periodic-notes:settings-updated' workspace event (fired on every settings.subscribe callback, i.e. every save) and calls reset(), which clears cachedFiles and re-runs initialize().
behaviour_notes: A full vault-tree rescan on every settings save (including a single keystroke in a format field, since PeriodicGroup's writable-derived store writes through to the parent settings store on each bound input) — a performance hazard on large vaults that a merge should consider debouncing.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity opt-in gate for prefix-matched notes
capabilities.description: In cache.resolve(), a filename's inexact/prefix match (isExactMatch===false from getDateWithPrefixFallback) is only accepted into the cache if that granularity's PeriodicConfig.allowPrefixMatch is true; an exact match is always accepted regardless.
behaviour_notes: Local fork addition, commit e50b8e8, default false — off by default so existing vaults don't suddenly start absorbing loosely-named files.

capabilities.name: Auto-apply the template to a manually-created empty file that matches a periodic pattern
capabilities.description: When resolve() is triggered by vault 'create' (not 'initialize') and the newly created file is empty (file.stat.size === 0), applyPeriodicTemplateToFile() renders and writes the granularity's template into it — so creating an empty file by hand with the right name (e.g. via 'New note') gets templated exactly as if openPeriodicNote had created it.
behaviour_notes: A quiet behavior easy to lose in a merge: this is the ONLY path that templates a file NOT created through createPeriodicNote/openPeriodicNote.
edge_cases: Does not fire during initialize() (reason !== 'create'), so pre-existing empty files at startup are never auto-templated, only ones created while the plugin is running.

capabilities.name: Override the global moment.js week-start day
capabilities.description: overrideGlobalMomentWeekStart(weekStart) saves the bundled locale's original week-spec once (window._bundledLocaleWeekSpec), then calls moment.updateLocale to either restore it ('locale') or force a specific day-of-week as dow.
behaviour_notes: This mutates the GLOBAL moment.js locale object shared by the whole Obsidian process — it affects every other plugin's date formatting too, and the settings UI says so explicitly ('may impact other plugins as well').

capabilities.name: One-time global moment.js locale configuration at plugin load
capabilities.description: configureGlobalMomentLocale(localeOverride, weekStart) maps Obsidian's UI language (or the user's explicit override, or a more-specific system locale) to a moment.js locale string and calls moment.locale(); initializeLocaleConfigOnce guards this to run only once per session via window._hasConfiguredLocale, regardless of how many times the plugin reloads.
behaviour_notes: The window._hasConfiguredLocale guard means DISABLING and RE-ENABLING the plugin within the same Obsidian session will not re-apply a changed localeOverride until a full reload — a subtle staleness trap.

capabilities.name: Human-readable relative date/period labels
capabilities.description: getRelativeDate(granularity, date): for 'week', special-cases this/last/next week then falls back to moment.duration(...).humanize(true); for 'day', uses moment's calendar() with custom lastWeek/lastDay/sameDay/nextDay/nextWeek/sameElse formatters; for month/quarter/year, plain date.format(HUMANIZE_FORMAT[granularity]).

capabilities.name: Settings mini-app breadcrumb router
capabilities.description: The `router` writable store holds a breadcrumb path (['Periodic Notes'] or ['Periodic Notes', <calendarSetId>]) plus an eState bag; navigate()/reset() drive which page Router.svelte renders and can carry one-shot flags (e.g. shouldRename) read by the destination page's onMount.
behaviour_notes: reset() is called from Router.svelte's onDestroy, i.e. whenever the settings tab is closed — so reopening settings always starts back at the dashboard, never resumes on the last-viewed calendar set.

capabilities.name: Settings dashboard: list, add calendar sets, global toggles
capabilities.description: Dashboard.svelte shows the getting-started banner (if not dismissed), a grid of calendar-set cards with a '+' to add one, the 'enable timeline complication' toggle, and the vault-wide week-start/locale dropdowns.

capabilities.name: Settings details page: rename, activate/duplicate/delete, per-granularity accordion
capabilities.description: Details.svelte for one calendar set: inline-editable title (rename), an 'Active' badge, an options menu (set active / duplicate / delete, delete disabled if it's the only set), and one PeriodicGroup accordion row per granularity.
behaviour_notes: Contains the local fork's scroll-guard crash fix (see observation) at onMount.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Format setting
capabilities.description: NoteFormatSetting.svelte: text input bound to calendarSets[].<g>.format; shows a live moment.js preview and validation error/complexity warning.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Note Folder setting
capabilities.description: NoteFolderSetting.svelte: text input with FolderSuggest autocomplete, bound to calendarSets[].<g>.folder, validated on blur.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Note Template setting
capabilities.description: NoteTemplateSetting.svelte: text input with FileSuggest autocomplete, bound to calendarSets[].<g>.templatePath, validated on blur.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Open on startup toggle
capabilities.description: OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte: toggle bound to calendarSets[].<g>.openAtStartup; turning it on first calls clearStartupNote across the whole settings tree.

capabilities.name: Per-granularity Allow prefix matching toggle
capabilities.description: AllowPrefixMatchSetting.svelte: toggle bound to calendarSets[].<g>.allowPrefixMatch, with an inline example in its description.
behaviour_notes: Local fork addition (commit e50b8e8), modeled directly on OpenAtStartupSetting.svelte's structure; no upstream equivalent.

capabilities.name: Detect and offer to migrate away from the core Daily Notes plugin
capabilities.description: GettingStartedBanner.svelte checks isDailyNotesPluginEnabled()/hasLegacyDailyNoteSettings() and, if the core plugin is enabled, offers a 'Disable' button (disableDailyNotesPlugin) with a reminder to update hotkeys.

capabilities.name: Natural-language date switcher
capabilities.description: 'Show date switcher...' opens NLDNavigator, a SuggestModal that (a) tries a small set of hand-written regex shortcuts (next/last/this <weekday|week|month|year>, 'in N units'/'N units ago', and bare today/yesterday/tomorrow/this-last-next week/month/year), filtered to active granularities and startsWith-matched against the query; (b) otherwise defers to the nldates-obsidian plugin's parseDate() for free-text parsing, then infers a granularity from the query text (week/month/quarter/year keyword, else day).
behaviour_notes: Only registered as a command when app.plugins.getPlugin('nldates-obsidian') exists (checked in checkCallback) — this whole capability is inert without that third-party plugin installed.

Cmd/Ctrl+Enter opens the selected item without closing the modal chooser's own key handling — implemented by reaching into the private, unexposed `this.chooser` via an `any` cast (obsidian.d.ts doesn't type it), a fragile dependency on Obsidian's internal SuggestModal implementation.
edge_cases: Quarter suggestions are commented out throughout ('TODO include once nldates supports quarters') — quarter notes are reachable only via the calendar sets UI/commands, not via this switcher's quick suggestions.

capabilities.name: Related-files switcher with modal hand-off
capabilities.description: Pressing Tab inside NLDNavigator closes it and opens RelatedFilesSwitcher scoped to the currently-selected date/granularity, listing every inexact-matched note for that period (optionally including finer granularities via Shift+8). Pressing Tab again closes it and reopens NLDNavigator, replaying the original query text via a synthetic 'input' event.
behaviour_notes: This chain (close-modal-A, open-modal-B, replay-query-via-synthetic-event) is stateful UI glue with no test coverage visible in the repo — a straightforward place to silently break during a merge if either modal's constructor signature or the 'Tab' scope registration changes.

capabilities.name: Quick-switch active calendar set via fuzzy modal
capabilities.description: CalendarSetSuggestModal (a FuzzySuggestModal) lists all calendar sets by id; selecting one calls setActiveSet.
behaviour_notes: getItemText() calls `item.toString()` on a CalendarSet object (relying on default Object toString / '[object Object]' fallback quirks are avoided only because Obsidian's FuzzySuggestModal actually calls getItemText for both matching AND fallback rendering) — this looks like it should be `item.id`; works today only because renderSuggestion overrides the visible text.

capabilities.name: Generic popper-positioned text-input autocomplete
capabilities.description: TextInputSuggest (abstract base) plus FileSuggest/FolderSuggest: wires an input's focus/input/blur events to a Suggest dropdown positioned via @popperjs/core, with arrow-key navigation and a shared Obsidian Scope pushed/popped on open/close.
behaviour_notes: FileSuggest/FolderSuggest do no fuzzy ranking — plain case-insensitive substring `contains()` filtering, unbounded (renders every match, no result cap), which could get slow in very large vaults.

capabilities.name: Timeline complication badge and week strip
capabilities.description: Timeline.svelte renders a small badge (relative date label, e.g. 'Today'/'Last week', plus a forward-arrow icon if the note was only inexactly matched) fixed top-right of any open periodic note; clicking expands a 7-day strip (starting the note's locale week) with the note's own day highlighted and today marked; clicking a day opens/creates that day's note. Controlled by the enableTimelineComplication setting and re-checked on file-open and cache-resolve events.
edge_cases: Nothing renders at all if the current view's file isn't found in the cache (cache.find returns null) — periodicData stays null and the {#if} guard hides the whole complication.

capabilities.name: Mount/unmount one Timeline component per open markdown leaf
capabilities.description: TimelineManager listens for workspace 'layout-change', diffs the set of open MarkdownView containerEls against its own tracked Svelte component instances, destroys ones whose leaf closed, and mounts a new Timeline into any view that doesn't have one yet.
behaviour_notes: cleanup() (called from plugin.unload) destroys every tracked component but does NOT unregister the 'layout-change' listener itself directly — that's handled by Obsidian's registerEvent auto-cleanup on plugin unload, not by this class.
edge_cases: Matching a Svelte component to its leaf is done by comparing `$$.root` (an internal Svelte instance field) to the view's containerEl — relies on undocumented Svelte internals rather than a public API.

flows.title: Open today's note from the ribbon icon
flows.description: User clicks the single ribbon icon shown for the first active granularity; if today's note for that granularity doesn't exist yet it is created (with template applied) before opening.
flows.trigger: user clicks the ribbon icon (or meta/cmd-clicks to open in a new split)

steps.action: getActiveGranularities() to know which icon to show
look up today's note for the active calendar set
createPeriodicNote() if not found, applying the template

flows.title: Create a note for an arbitrary date via the natural-language date switcher
flows.description: User runs 'Show date switcher...' and types a free-text date; the plugin resolves it (via its own regex shortcuts or the nldates-obsidian plugin) and opens/creates the corresponding periodic note.
flows.trigger: user runs the 'Show date switcher...' command and types e.g. 'next friday'

steps.action: open NLDNavigator (only if nldates-obsidian is installed)

flows.title: Switch the active calendar set
flows.description: User runs 'Switch active calendar set...', picks another set from the fuzzy list; the active set changes, commands/ribbon are re-registered for the new set's granularities, and the note cache is rebuilt.
flows.trigger: user runs the 'Switch active calendar set...' command

steps.action: configureCommands() + configureRibbonIcons() for the new active set

flows.title: Edit a granularity's filename format in settings
flows.description: User opens the plugin's settings tab, drills into a calendar set, expands a granularity's group, and edits the Format field; validation runs live, the change is written straight into calendarSets[], and the cache rebuilds.
flows.trigger: user opens Settings > Periodic Notes > a calendar set > expands e.g. 'Daily Notes' > edits Format

steps.action: mount SettingsRouter into the settings tab
render Details for the selected calendar set
render NoteFormatSetting bound to a writable-derived config store
cache.reset() fires on the resulting settings-updated event

flows.title: Jump to a related note via the date switcher's Tab hand-off
flows.description: From the natural-language date switcher, pressing Tab opens a second modal listing every inexactly-matched ('related') note for the selected period, optionally widened to finer granularities.
flows.trigger: user presses Tab while a date suggestion is highlighted in NLDNavigator

steps.action: close self, open RelatedFilesSwitcher with the selected item + query
leaf.openFile() on the chosen related note

flows.title: Open the timeline complication and jump to a weekday
flows.description: Every open periodic note shows a small relative-date badge top-right; clicking it expands a 7-day strip, and clicking a day opens (or creates) that day's note.
flows.trigger: user clicks the timeline badge on an open periodic note, then clicks a weekday

steps.action: instantiate Timeline.svelte into the view's containerEl on layout-change
cache.find(view.file.path) to get the relative label and week
createPeriodicNote()/getPeriodicNote() when a weekday is clicked

flows.title: Jump forwards/backwards to the closest existing periodic note
flows.description: From an existing periodic note, run 'Jump forwards/backwards to closest <periodicity> note' to navigate to the nearest existing note of the same granularity in that direction, without creating anything if none exists.
flows.trigger: user runs 'Jump forwards to closest daily note' on an active periodic note

flows.title: Open the next/previous periodic note by date offset, creating it if missing
flows.description: From an existing periodic note, run 'Open next daily note' to always land on that date's note, creating it (with template) if it doesn't exist.
flows.trigger: user runs 'Open next daily note' on an active periodic note

flows.title: Auto-open a configured note on vault load
flows.description: If any granularity in any calendar set has 'Open at startup' enabled, that note is opened (created if missing) as soon as the workspace layout is ready.
flows.trigger: Obsidian finishes loading the vault's workspace layout

flows.title: Create a new calendar set and configure a granularity
flows.description: User clicks '+' next to 'Calendar Sets' on the dashboard, is dropped straight into the new set's Details page with the title ready to rename, then enables and configures a granularity.
flows.trigger: user clicks the '+' icon in the settings dashboard

steps.action: mount Details, focus the rename field on mount

flows.title: Rename a calendar set inline
flows.description: User edits the contenteditable title on a calendar set's Details page and blurs it; the id is validated and updated, and (if it was the active set) activeCalendarSet is updated too.
flows.trigger: user clicks the calendar-set title in Details, edits the text, clicks elsewhere

steps.action: router.navigate to the new id on success

flows.title: Migrate legacy Daily Notes settings on first load
flows.description: The very first time the plugin loads with no calendarSets[] saved, it inspects the raw saved data and the core Daily Notes plugin to synthesize a starting 'Default' calendar set instead of starting empty.
flows.trigger: plugin loads for the first time (or after data.json was reset) with an empty calendarSets[]

steps.action: migrateLegacySettingsToCalendarSet() or migrateDailyNoteSettings(), else a bare default

flows.title: Recognize a prefix-named note by enabling 'Allow prefix matching'
flows.description: A file like '2026-W07, 09.02 - 15.02.md' doesn't strictly match the configured weekly format 'gggg-[W]ww'. Enabling 'Allow prefix matching' for that granularity makes the cache accept it as that week's note.
flows.trigger: user toggles 'Allow prefix matching' on for the weekly granularity

steps.action: getDateWithPrefixFallback() now allowed to win for this granularity

flows.title: Duplicate an existing calendar set
flows.description: User opens the '...' menu on a calendar-set card and picks 'Duplicate calendar set'; a new set with a '<name> copy' id and the same per-granularity config is created and opened for renaming.
flows.trigger: user clicks '...' on a calendar-set card, then 'Duplicate calendar set'

steps.action: router.navigate to the new set with shouldRename: true

observations.what: Local fork guards the settings-tab scroll call against a missing '.vertical-tab-content' element.
observations.why_it_matters: Obsidian 1.13 changed the settings-modal DOM; without the optional-chaining guard, opening the plugin's settings tab throws ('Cannot read properties of undefined (reading scroll)') and leaves the Svelte component half-mounted, breaking the whole settings UI. A merge must carry this guard forward or the crash reappears on current Obsidian.

observations.what: Local fork adds an 'allowPrefixMatch' setting and its whole vertical slice.
observations.why_it_matters: Not present upstream (liamcain/obsidian-periodic-notes). A merge that starts from upstream code will silently lose prefix-matching for notes whose filenames only start with the configured format (e.g. weekly notes with a trailing date-range suffix).

observations.what: Local fork replaced a bare JSON module import with fs.readFileSync + JSON.parse in the esbuild config, and pinned Node 24.12.0.
observations.why_it_matters: Node 24 rejects an unattributed JSON module import (ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING); without this change the build breaks on the fork's own pinned toolchain. A merged build script for the whole family must pick one convention for reading manifest.json, and honor (or explicitly override) the Node version pin.

observations.what: Local fork dropped 'yarn run lint' from the production build script.
observations.why_it_matters: svelte-check 2.7.0 can't parse this repo's inline type-only import specifiers ('import { type X }'), a pre-existing toolchain mismatch, so the fork bypassed the gate rather than fixing it. A merged repo needs a working lint/typecheck step or will silently reintroduce type errors.

observations.what: Top-level per-granularity settings keys (daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly/yearly) exist only inside a private, migration-only type — not in the live settings interface used at runtime.
where: src/calendarSetManager.ts:20-30 (ILegacySettings — has them, but this type is only used by isLegacySettings()/migrateLegacySettingsToCalendarSet(), called exactly once from src/main.ts:177-187 during loadSettings())
observations.why_it_matters: A merge that assumes v0.0.17 still reads/writes top-level daily/weekly/... settings (as much older versions of this plugin, and possibly sibling repos in this family, do) will be targeting dead code. The only live, ongoing config surface in this fork is calendarSets[]; the top-level keys are read exactly once, from raw loaded JSON, purely to detect a pre-upgrade vault.

observations.what: The Locale dropdown in the settings dashboard writes its value to the wrong Obsidian vault-config key.
observations.why_it_matters: Both the 'Start week on' and 'Locale' dropdowns call app.vault.setConfig('weekStart', val) — the Locale handler is a copy-paste of the week-start handler and never writes 'localeOverride'. Changing Locale in the UI never actually persists a locale override (it just re-writes weekStart with the locale-dropdown's value instead), while configureGlobalMomentLocale() at load time correctly reads 'localeOverride' from vault config — so the bug is invisible until you try to change locale live and reload.

observations.what: ISettings carries several fields nothing reads at runtime.
observations.why_it_matters: Declared and defaulted but never read again anywhere else in the source (confirmed by grep). localeOverride/weekStart are additionally shadowed by the real values living in Obsidian's vault-level config, not plugin data.json. A merge should not port these fields as if they carried live state.

observations.what: FileOptionsSwitcher, PeriodicNoteCreateModal and IconButton.svelte are defined but never instantiated or imported anywhere in the source.
where: src/modal.ts:27-74 (PeriodicNoteCreateModal class only — showFileMenu in the same file IS used)
observations.why_it_matters: None of the three is reachable from any command, event, or component in this repo (confirmed by grep for each class/component name). Do not port these as capabilities; they are inert leftovers — fileOptionsSwitcher.ts's own 'Delete file' item even has an empty onChooseSuggestion body.

observations.what: MatchType's 'date-prefixed' variant is declared but never produced.
observations.why_it_matters: Only 'filename' and 'frontmatter' are ever assigned to matchData.matchType anywhere in the source. Harmless, but a porting agent should not build logic that expects this variant to occur.

observations.what: Frontmatter-based note resolution ignores the calendar set's configured format and its allowPrefixMatch flag, unlike the filename-based path.
observations.why_it_matters: resolve() (filename matching) correctly uses getPossibleFormats() + getDateWithPrefixFallback() against the user's configured format. resolveChangedMetadata() (frontmatter matching) instead hard-codes DEFAULT_FORMAT[granularity] for the strict parse. A note identified only via frontmatter (e.g. `day: 2022-02-02`) with a non-default format configured will silently fail to resolve. A merged note-resolution engine should unify these two code paths rather than keep the asymmetry.

observations.what: The vault-wide loose date-fallback in cache.resolve() is not scoped to any calendar set's configured folder.
observations.why_it_matters: When no active granularity's folder+format matches a file, resolve() falls through to getLooselyMatchedDate(file.basename) with no folder check at all. Any markdown file anywhere in the vault whose basename merely contains a YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM/YYYY-shaped substring (e.g. '2026 Meeting Notes.md') gets cached as an inexact match for every calendar set that has active granularities, which can surface as incorrect '+N related notes' badges and pollute the related-files switcher with unrelated files.

observations.what: No monkey-patching of Obsidian's built-in Quick Switcher exists anywhere in src/switcher/*; the real hazard is the stateful hand-off between two custom modals.
observations.why_it_matters: A grep for prototype/monkey/patch/QuickSwitcher across src/ found nothing. All four 'switcher' classes are independent SuggestModal/FuzzySuggestModal subclasses (Obsidian's own public modal API), opened from the plugin's own commands — not modifications of core UI. The actual merge hazard is the Tab hand-off between NLDNavigator and RelatedFilesSwitcher (closing one modal, opening the other, and replaying the query string via a synthetic 'input' event) — that chain has no test coverage and is easy to break silently if either constructor's signature changes during a merge.

observations.what: The assignment's description of where openPeriodicNote/getDateWithPrefixFallback live doesn't match the code exactly.
observations.why_it_matters: openPeriodicNote is a PeriodicNotesPlugin method in main.ts, not utils.ts. utils.ts does correctly hold getDateWithPrefixFallback and the rest of the date/template helpers. Noted so a porting agent doesn't waste time searching utils.ts for openPeriodicNote.

observations.what: getPeriodicNotes' own author flags its shape as unsettled.
where: src/main.ts:239 (inline comment: '// TODO: What API do I want for this?')
observations.why_it_matters: Treat this method's signature (a boolean includeFinerGranularities flag) as a redesign candidate in the merged plugin rather than a contract that must be preserved exactly.

observations.what: Cross-plugin lookup by manifest id will fail for this specific vault install.
observations.why_it_matters: The assignment states this fork is installed under the dev plugin id 'periodic-notes-anks'. Any other plugin (e.g. obsidian-calendar-plugin) calling app.plugins.getPlugin('periodic-notes') gets undefined in this vault, even though the code and its public methods are otherwise present and working. This is an install-time integration risk specific to this vault, not a code bug — worth flagging before testing the merged plugin's cross-plugin API here.

observations.what: Week-start day-of-week helpers are re-implemented three separate times within this one repo.
observations.why_it_matters: Three separate hard-coded ['sunday'..'saturday'] arrays with slightly different rotation logic for locale week-start. A merge across this whole plugin family should consolidate on one canonical day-of-week utility rather than porting all three independently.
